summary: Mini's third-generation electric Cooper hatch is, by broad Australian reviewer consensus, the most entertaining EV in its price bracket — CarsGuide scored the driving experience a perfect 10 and Chasing Cars called it one of the most enjoyable electric cars on sale here — but the same reviewers keep landing on the same objection: it is a very small, very expensive car. Mini Australia deleted the cheaper Cooper E in 2025, so the range now opens at $58,990 before on-road costs for the 400km Cooper SE, roughly $20,000 above an equivalently sized MG 4. Opinion splits hardest on the ride: some testers treat the taut, fidgety damping as part of the go-kart appeal, others find it wearing on suburban roads, and the JCW E does without the adaptive dampers the petrol JCW gets.
pros: Genuinely engaging chassis — sharp steering and go-kart agility that no other electric hatch near the price matches, per CarsGuide (10/10 driving) and Chasing Cars
Quick for a small hatch: 160kW/330Nm and 0-100km/h in 6.7s in the Cooper SE, 190kW and 5.9s in the JCW E
The 9.4-inch circular OLED touchscreen is a real design statement rather than a generic tablet, and reviewers rate the interface fast and genuinely fun to use
Every variant sits well under the $75,000 FBT exemption cap, so a novated-lease buyer keeps the exemption even on the top JCW E at $63,990
High-voltage battery covered for 8 years on top of the 5-year unlimited-kilometre vehicle warranty
cons: 210-litre boot is among the smallest of any EV on sale in Australia — under half the 470 litres of a Skoda Elroq, and only 800 litres with the rear seats folded
Strictly a four-seater with token rear legroom; CarExpert's 185cm tester could not sit behind his own driving position, and CarsGuide called the rear backrests too upright for adults
Real-world consumption of 17-18kWh/100km against the 14.7kWh/100km claim drops usable range to roughly 300km from the 49.2kWh battery
Expensive for the metal: an MG 4 Essence 64 is $37,510 and a Tesla Model 3 RWD $54,900, both far more practical, and Mini offers only one interior trim on the SE
95kW peak DC charging is modest — 30 minutes for 10-80 per cent, where similarly priced rivals manage well over 100kW
